purpose: Reconcile the prior session's flip-diagnosis-report.md claims against the raw data files it cites, and root-cause the discrepancy, per the 2026-07-20 corrective-loop directive sections 1, 2, and 6.

bugs_found.description: apex_t (the natural, pre-ignition apogee used to bound the descent-analysis window) was computed as argmax(altitude) over the WHOLE flight trace, not the first local apogee. A retro burn that fires close enough to the natural apogee to still be climbing can impart enough net-upward impulse to create a second, HIGHER altitude peak later in the flight. argmax(altitude) then silently selects that later, post-burn peak as 'the apex'. Every downstream filter of the form 'if t < apex_t: continue' (descent_profile in scripts/descent_gates.py, and the ignition/burn-window search in flip_diagnosis.py) then discards the ENTIRE burn window, because the miscomputed apex_t falls after burnout.

measured_example.effect: burn_mean_q and i_opp_over_i_total both computed as null, making a motor that ignited exactly on schedule and delivered 736 N peak thrust look like it never fired

bugs_found.fix: scripts/descent_gates.py::apex_time_from_apogee_events() reads OpenRocket's own APOGEE FlightEvent (first/minimum time), falling back to argmax(altitude) only if no APOGEE event exists. Both call sites updated.

bugs_found.description: A second, distinct failure mode found while verifying the first fix: if ignition happens AT OR BEFORE the natural free-fall apogee, the burn's added impulse can delay the POWERED branch's own single true APOGEE event past burnout entirely (the branch genuinely does not stop climbing, by OpenRocket's own vertical-velocity-sign criterion, until well after the motor has burned out). Recomputing apex_t from the powered branch's own event -- even via the corrected apex_time_from_apogee_events() -- still discards the whole burn window in this case, because that event is a property of the POWERED (perturbed) trajectory, not the unpowered one the descent-window filter is supposed to bound.

measured_example.effect: burn_mean_q and i_opp_over_i_total again computed as null, because the burn window (8.736-10.431s) is entirely before the powered branch's own (delayed) apogee event at 15.128s

bugs_found.fix: run_ork() now accepts an optional apex_t_hint; every powered probe of a candidate reuses the already-known, uncorrupted free-descent run's own apex_t instead of recomputing one from the (perturbed) powered branch. run_ork() still reports own_apex_t and used_apex_t_hint for auditability.

bugs_found.description: min_speed_after_ignition took an unfiltered min() over speed_ms across the whole post-ignition trace. OpenRocket zeroes velocity (and this script's trace records q=None) at and after GROUND_HIT, so the unfiltered min() always selected that zeroed ground-hit/post-impact sample (speed_ms=0.0, q=null) rather than any genuine near-hover point during the actual flight -- for 3 of the 4 delays in the original run (9.8s, 10.0s, 15.0s).
bugs_found.fix: Extracted scripts/flip_diagnosis.py::_min_speed_after_ignition(), which excludes samples at/after GROUND_HIT, samples with null q, and samples before ignition.

section_6_ignition_gap_resolution.prior_claim: flip-diagnosis-report.md Finding 4 claimed delays 8.5-9.2s on the K550W-default E8_8 topology 'silently never ignite' (thrust stays at 0 for the whole flight), attributed to 'a real engine/config quantization or arming-condition gap in osifog_sweep.py's retro-delay wiring'.
section_6_ignition_gap_resolution.investigation: Dense 11-point sweep (8.50-9.50s, 0.1s steps) on the exact K550W/E8_8 topology, with the apex-detection fix applied. See artifacts/autoevo/ignition-window-resolution.json for full per-delay event traces.
section_6_ignition_gap_resolution.result: 11/11 delays ignited exactly on schedule (observed IGNITION event time == requested delay to the millisecond, e.g. requested 8.90 -> observed 8.9000). Peak thrust after the requested delay was 750-800 N in every case. 0/11 'genuinely never ignited'.
section_6_ignition_gap_resolution.conclusion: Finding 4 is FALSE. There is no ignition-arming-window gap in osifog_sweep.py. The 'silent non-ignition' Finding 4 reported was entirely an artifact of the apex-detection bug above: for delays close to the natural apogee, the analysis script's own apex_t was miscomputed as a later time (a second altitude peak, or the powered branch's own delayed apogee event), which made the ignition-search loop's 't > apex_t' condition fail to find real, on-schedule ignition and thrust. No fix to osifog_sweep.py's ignition/delay wiring was needed or made; only the two analysis-script bugs above were fixed.

strake_batch_prior_session.report_claim: flip-diagnosis-report.md Finding 6 stated 'this session's whole gated batch used 4 powered OpenRocket evaluations (all correctly early-stopped within 2 runs each)'.
strake_batch_prior_session.note_on_16_vs_4_discrepancy: artifacts/autoevo/strake-batch-results.json (the report's own cited raw data) contains 16 powered_probes entries across 7 candidates (2+3+3+3+3+2+0), not 4. The report's table additionally mislabeled 4 of those 16 as 'not tested (ascent-illegal)' when the JSON shows they were tested (3 powered OpenRocket probes each, real final_speed_ms values recorded) -- the admission gate in scripts/descent_gates.py::passive_descent_admission never checks ascent margin at all (by design: it is a descent-only gate; ascent legality is a separate, independent precondition per the mission's live-insert instruction), so ascent-illegal strake-only candidates were correctly descent-admitted and consumed real powered OpenRocket evaluations. All 16 of those probes additionally had burn_mean_q=null and i_opp_over_i_total=null due to the apex-detection bugs above, which is almost certainly why the report's author (mis)read them as 'not tested' rather than 'tested but with corrupted burn telemetry'.
strake_batch_prior_session.verdict: The reported '78x reduction' and '4 powered evaluations' claims in flip-diagnosis-report.md Finding 6 are not supported by its own cited data file and must not be relied on.

strake_batch_this_session_corrected_reru.note: With both apex-detection bugs fixed, every admitted candidate's FIRST powered probe now yields real (non-null) i_opp_over_i_total, so PoweredEarlyStop's impulse-fraction threshold check fires immediately for all 6 admitted candidates (one probe each) instead of needing 2-3 probes per candidate as before. This is a genuine, verified reduction, not a reporting artifact: 6 real powered evaluations across 6 admitted candidates + 0 for the 1 descent-rejected candidate = 6 total, all with valid non-null burn telemetry. Current data: artifacts/autoevo/strake-batch-results.json (regenerated this session).

flip_diagnosis_prior_and_this_session.note: These delays (all >=9.5s, well after this topology's natural apogee at 8.485s) were NOT affected by the apex-detection bugs -- re-running them post-fix reproduces the original Findings 2/3/5 q/direction-cosine numbers to within rounding. Only min_speed_after_ignition changed (ground-contact contamination fix), now showing genuine in-flight minima instead of post-impact zeros.
